question: Why does healthcare use special United Nations packaging requirements for moving specimens?

options.A: Reducing the overall cost of medical courier services
options.B: Simplifying hospital inventory control for plastic containers
options.C: Preventing leaks and exposure during specimen transit
options.D: Accelerating laboratory turnaround time for test results

explanation: Specialized packaging standards exist specifically to contain hazardous biological or chemical contents and protect handlers from exposure risks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: When sending blood samples via courier, why can standard hospital paperwork not replace formal UN transport documents?

options.A: Doctors prefer keeping physical charts inside the specimen cooler
options.B: Laboratory software cannot print documents on waterproof paper
options.C: Courier companies refuse to read standard hospital clinical charts
options.D: Clinical forms lack hazard classifications required for transport safety

explanation: Transport regulations mandate specific hazard details and emergency response data that standard clinical requisition forms do not provide. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: Which UN number is assigned to routine Category B biological diagnostic specimens?
explanation: UN 3373 is the universal designation specifically reserved for biological substances transported in Category B diagnostic quantities. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h2)

question: What makes a biological agent count as a Category A infectious substance?

options.A: Capability of causing permanent disability or fatal disease upon exposure
options.B: Requirement to be frozen in liquid nitrogen throughout the journey
options.C: Origin exclusively from veterinary research facilities and slaughterhouses
options.D: Resistance to standard hospital chemical disinfectants and heat

explanation: Category A is reserved for high-consequence pathogens that pose severe, life-threatening risks if containment fails during transit. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h2)

question: What is the job of the absorbent material inside the secondary packaging?

options.A: Soaking up the entire liquid contents if the primary container breaks
options.B: Neutralizing hazardous chemical fumes before they reach the outer box
options.C: Preventing the primary glass tube from freezing during air transport
options.D: Maintaining a cold internal temperature for perishable blood samples

explanation: Absorbent padding is placed inside the secondary layer to completely retain any spilled fluid and prevent seepage outside the package. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h3)

question: A nurse places a blood vial directly into a cardboard shipping box without secondary wrapping. Which safety layer of the triple packaging system is missing?
explanation: The secondary layer provides an intermediate leak-proof barrier and housing for absorbent material between the primary vial and the outer box. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h3)

question: What does the code '4G' at the start of a UN packaging mark mean?
explanation: The number 4 designates a box, and the letter G specifies that the material used in construction is fiberboard. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h4)

question: Why must clinics only use boxes with official UN specification codes for infectious shipments?

options.A: Certified boxes have successfully passed strict physical stress and drop tests
options.B: Customs officials refuse to process unbranded cardboard boxes of any kind
options.C: Standard clinic storage boxes degrade quickly under fluorescent lighting
options.D: Manufacturers give legal guarantees against all carrier shipping delays

explanation: The UN stamp serves as physical verification that the container design withstood engineering trials simulating transport accidents. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h4)

question: Which diamond-shaped mark goes on the outside of a package carrying Category B specimens?
explanation: The square-on-point diamond containing the number 3373 is the mandatory universal identifier for Category B biological shipments. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h5)

question: What essential contact detail must be included with a dangerous goods transport package?

options.A: Direct emergency line to the local fire department station dispatcher
options.B: Home address of the patient whose blood is inside the primary vial
options.C: Name and telephone number of a person knowledgeable about the shipment
options.D: Personal email and office number of the hospital chief executive officer

explanation: Carriers and emergency responders require a designated knowledgeable contact to provide immediate guidance if a spill or delay occurs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h5)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility when preparing diagnostic specimens for off-site transport?

options.A: Certifying the structural drop-test rating of the outer cardboard box
options.B: Applying chemical sterilants to the exterior of the outer shipping box
options.C: Ensuring primary container lids are tightly sealed to prevent leaks
options.D: Personally driving the transport vehicle to the destination laboratory

explanation: The nurse initiating the specimen collection must verify primary closure integrity to prevent fluid escape during transit. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h6)

question: A nurse runs out of secondary containers and thinks about using a sealed polythene shopping bag for blood tubes. What is the main problem with this action?

options.A: Couriers will charge extra administrative fees for non-standard baggage shapes
options.B: Laboratory automated analyzers cannot open plastic grocery bags safely
options.C: Plastic shopping bags are environmentally unfriendly for medical establishments
options.D: Polythene bags lack the leak-proof durability and absorption standards required for transit

explanation: Improvising with non-compliant bags violates containment regulations and increases the risk of unabsorbed spills during transit. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h6)
